renderings.value: The ～ば～のに grammar point is used to express regret or dissatisfaction about a situation that didn't happen or to express a contrary view of the actual situation. It can be translated as 'if only' or 'wish' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
Verb-ば form + ～のに, い-Adjective-ば form + ～のに, な-Adjective + であれば + ～のに, Noun + であれば + ～のに
Regretful - "if only X, (but reality is otherwise)".
Wish And Hope (I Hope / If Only)
If only I had come earlier, I would have made it to the train.
I wish I had studied more, I would have passed the exam.
If only she were kinder, she would get along with him.
I wish I were good at Japanese, then I could read this book.
